F11.title: Derivation accepts trailing payload and does not check contiguity or the last block; L1 counts are discarded; the parent lbn is not in the public input.

F12.title: Codec domains, missing v2 encoder, ineffective cache, genesis cursor, downgrade, legacy hash, uint16 accumulators, documentation drift.

F14.title: Batches can be committed at a version and index the router cannot resolve.

F2.title: Revert preserves the blob hash; recommits must reuse it, including a "no blob" Z or a malformed blob.

F3.title: The Go blob-retrieval error path indexes out of bounds for non-canonical elements at index ≥ 3968.

F4.title: Unsigned underflow in challenge arithmetic disables all commits once a challenge is stale.

F5.title: A challenge on any batch reopens a proof-backed batch's window.

F6.title: A recommit can change the version while reusing a blob hash of different meaning.

F7.title: The delay guard reads the finalization cursor instead of the inclusion cursor (reconciled as a profile).

F8.title: Third parties can exhaust the replay budget; the fee waiver is keyed on the original sender.

F9.title: Estimators assume compression never expands; one omits contexts; slice aliasing.

N1.title: η₂ wrote CSR only at the last committed index. Suppose:

N2.title: Cancelling a challenge leaves the +W extensions it applied to other batches. An intent contract (§5.9) can bound this as designed behaviour.

N3.title: Under the BVH pin, the content of the recommitted batch is fixed by the original submitter S₁, while the bond at risk is the recommitter S₂'s. A rational S₂ therefore refuses to recommit unprovable content, which turns slashing into a liveness deterrent.

N4.title: Legacy committers cannot prove their own in-flight batches after the cutover. If no prover in the new registry acts within W, a possibly valid batch is reverted.
